_comment: Expectation manifest for the frozen acceptance-checks under evals/checks/.
Enforced by evals/floor/06-checks-manifest.test.mjs, so it runs on the whetstone baseline AND
after every kept item — which is what makes a past fix's regression loud instead of invisible.
expect 'green' = a past item whose fix must not regress. MUST exit 0.
expect 'red'   = a known-failing check: an open concern or an in-flight item. MUST exit 0 or 1,
never >=2 (>=2 is harness rot: the check failed to run, e.g. a generator flag
it passes became invalid). A 'red' check that turns GREEN does NOT fail the
floor -- the floor gates the whetstone loop, so an exact-match rule would
revert the very fix that resolves the concern. The floor prints a promote-me
notice instead; move it to 'green' when its fix lands.
LOCKED (evals/**): the whetstone fixer may never edit this file. That is the point -- otherwise
the loop could flip a regressing check to 'red' and escape its own fence.

book-under-flag.note: Twice-fixed, now guarded. Fixed once (2826 -> 1479 words), silently re-accreted to 2469 across seven runs, then re-shrunk by the consolidate pass in PR #37. Promoted to 'green' on 2026-07-25 so a THIRD re-accretion breaks the floor instead of decaying unnoticed -- which is the whole reason this manifest exists.

dead-item-worker-recorded-as-done.note: Fixed by whetstone run conductor-fanout-cluster (8057005), promoted 2026-07-30. A dead item worker is recorded ok:false and noted in results.coverage; checkpoint persists the notes and marks the run partial; Writeup renders 'Coverage and uncertainty'. Only a level where NOTHING landed still throws -- there is no diff to integrate and every later level would branch off a base missing the whole level. Continuing past a PARTIAL death is safe only because dodgate-plan-of-record's plan verifier adjudicates every planned item against the real diff; do not weaken that check thinking this one covers it.

dodgate-plan-of-record.note: Added 2026-07-30 together with its fix, so it lands as 'green'. Verified RED (7/9) against the origin/main@d5e5b25 generator via GEN_OVERRIDE before landing -- it discriminates, it is not a check that passes on nothing. Guards two drift paths a frozen DoD structurally cannot see: a worker retiring its own planned item, and parallel() returning null for a dead worker (which the baseline recorded as a completed item carrying an empty summary).

dynamic-fanout-within-phase.note: SUCCESSOR CHECK -- also carries the protection of two concerns whose own checks were retired in PR #38 because they asserted the pre-#40 doctrine: 'independent-work-needs-per-worker-worktrees' (per-item worktree isolation -> assertion 6) and 'parallelize-independent-work-items' (work inside a phase must not be serial -> assertions 3-5, the parallel() batching). Do not weaken those assertions thinking they are redundant; nothing else guards them.

headless-driver-still-ends-turn.note: SUCCESSOR CHECK -- supersedes the earlier concern 'headless-background-workflow-orphan' (a headless -p driver backgrounded the workflow, ended its turn, and the exiting process killed the orphan). That fix is assertion 1 here (SKILL.md pins run_in_background: false); assertions 2-3 add the blocking-call and state-file re-verify requirements on top.

integrate-and-setup-trusted-on-a-bare-bo.note: Fixed by whetstone run conductor-fanout-cluster (9b3b188), promoted 2026-07-30. PLAN_SETUP_SCHEMA requires created:string[] and PLAN_INTEGRATE_SCHEMA requires merged_branches:string[]; a pure-JS planSetDiff() set-compares them against the dispatched worktree/branch sets and aborts the level naming the missing/extra entries. The prompts now ASK for the list and warn that padding it stops the run -- keep both halves: a schema nobody is told to fill returns nothing.

loop-decides-decomposition.note: Fixed by run conductor-20260725-093937 (2a401f5): --independent hard-errors, SKILL.md step 1d is gone, decomposition is documented as the runtime planner's job. Keeps the doctrine from drifting back: the human declares the goal + DoD, the loop decides the split.

plan-fanout-levels-never-checkpointed.note: Fixed by whetstone run conductor-fanout-cluster (43a3890), promoted 2026-07-30. results.<key>Levels records per-level integration plus per-item {id,title,ok,summary}; the checkpoint moved to the TOP of the level loop so it persists the plan on the first pass and each completed level after, with no extra call site. A resume skips levels already marked integrated and re-dispatches only items with no recorded ok. Shares the per-item ok flag with dead-item-worker-recorded-as-done by design.

trivial-phases-merged.note: Fixed 2026-07-29: a checkpoint exists to avoid re-running EXPENSIVE work, so the six phases that are cheap to re-run correctly (Setup, Brief, Verify, ReVerify, PR, TicketUpdate) no longer buy a dedicated checkpoint worker — 15 -> 9 per delivery run. DoDBaseline deliberately keeps its checkpoint despite running in seconds: re-running it on a resume after work had landed would record a post-work state as the pre-work baseline. The phase-MERGE half of the original concern was dropped, not implemented — frontend-gate-phase and dod-gate assert phase('ReVerify') and phase('DoDBaseline') exist, so a check demanding they disappear would contradict two green checks.
